importance_ranking.reason: Buyers have a specific aesthetic and shape brief — conical, dome, pagoda, and hypar forms are visually non-interchangeable. Image is the primary shape and colour sample; wrong shape or finish causes an immediate skip before any text is read.

Fabric material (PVC vs PTFE) and shape are non-interchangeable spec tiers that drive both price and suitability. Buyers shortlist on these specs before contacting any seller — a listing without them cannot be evaluated.

Indian hospitality and commercial buyers compare per-sq-ft rates aggressively across multiple sellers. Price varies substantially with fabric material (PVC vs PTFE), shape complexity, and size — making it a primary shortlisting signal after visual and spec confirmation.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Modular/standard-size units may be quoted per piece; large commercial installations may be quoted per project (lump sum). Per sq ft vs per piece creates real price comparison confusion — unit must be shown alongside price.
importance_ranking.reason: Three distinct quoting conventions exist in this market (per sq ft, per piece, per project). A buyer comparing listings across sellers cannot make a valid price comparison without knowing the unit — confusion is a real and documented risk.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant manufacturer brand with buyer recall exists in this category — market is fragmented across regional fabricators; buyers search by shape and spec, not by company name.
importance_ranking.reason: Custom supply-and-install purchase means buyers evaluate installation capability, completed project portfolio, and warranty support during vendor selection — but only after spec and price shortlisting. Company is a qualifier, not a primary signal.
